title: Building HTTP APIs with Azure Functions
description: Use HTTP triggers to build REST APIs with routing, status codes, and JSON responses in Azure Functions.

data.text: HTTP triggers are the most common trigger type for building APIs. They accept HTTP requests and return HTTP responses, making Azure Functions a lightweight alternative to full API frameworks.

items: Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, or specific combinations

OpenAPI Support
data.text: Azure Functions supports OpenAPI (Swagger) definitions through the `Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.OpenApi` package. This enables automatic API documentation and testing in the Azure portal.

data.title: Build a Simple GET API
data.description: Create an HTTP-triggered function that returns a JSON array of sample products.
steps: Create a function with HTTP trigger, GET method, route 'products'
Return a hardcoded list of 3 products as JSON
Add a route parameter for GET /products/{id}
data.expectedOutcome: The API returns valid JSON for both the list and single-item endpoints.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: HTTP triggers make Functions ideal for lightweight APIs
Return typed HTTP results for clarity
data.takeaway: Azure Functions is a simple way to build REST APIs without managing web servers.
